summary: Maurice Jametel (1856–1889) was a scholar in sinology and tibetology who studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes. He later taught Édouard Chavannes and held a post at the same institution from circa 1886 to 1889.
Maurice Lehot (d. 1931) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon under Félix Lacôte. He worked as a schoolteacher (Professor) at the Lycée d'Aix-en-Provence.

Linguist Maurice Leroy (1909–1990) studied at the Université libre de Bruxelles and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Theodor Bloch, Joseph Vendryes, and Émile Benveniste. He became a professor at Bruxelles in 1945 and Secrétaire perpétuel of the Royal Academy of Belgium.

Maurice O'Connell Walshe (1911–1998) worked in Buddhist studies and linguistics, studying at UCL, Berlin, Göttingen, and Vienna, and under Walpola Rahula. He taught at Freiburg, UCL, Leeds, Nottingham, and Bedford College, serving as Deputy Director at the University of London.

Maurice Phillips (1839–1910) was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Bedford College and the University of Bern. He served as a missionary with the London Missionary Society (1862–1908) and was a Fellow at the University of Madras (1892).
Maurice Wiles (1923–2005) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tonbridge School and Christ's College, Cambridge. He later taught Michael Pye.
Maurice Wilmotte (1861–1942) was a linguist who studied at the University of Liège from circa 1880 to 1885. He subsequently held a post at the University of Liège from circa 1895 to 1931.

Maurine Stuart (1922–1990) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Manitoba and under Nadia Boulanger, Eido Shimano, Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, and Soen Nakagawa. In 1979, she became president and spiritual director of the Cambridge Buddhist Association.

Maurizio Taddei (1936–2000) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Mario Bussagli at Sapienza University, working later at the Museo Nazionale d'Arte Orientale, University of Naples "L'Orientale", and IsIAO.

Mauro Maggi works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and under Ronald Eric Emmerick, holding posts at the Italian Institute for Africa and the East and Sapienza University of Rome.

Mavis L. Fenn specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the Universities of Winnipeg and Calgary and completed her Ph.D. under Graeme MacQueen at McMaster University, later holding posts at St. Paul's University College and the University of Waterloo.
Max Arthur Macauliffe (1841–1913) was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He completed his education at Springfield College and the University of Galway.

Max Deeg is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who completed his Habilitation at the University of Würzburg. He has held positions at Nagoya University, the University of Vienna, Cardiff University, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Max Hunter Harrison (1893–1986), an Indology and religious studies scholar, studied at Knox College, Andover Newton, Harvard, and Columbia. He taught at Jaffna College, served as Principal of United Theological College, Bangalore, and was acting director at the Missionary Research Library.

Linguist Max Jakob Niedermann (1874–1954) studied at Zurich and Basel under Jacob Wackernagel, Antoine Meillet, Louis Havet, and Rudolf Thurneysen. He held teaching and professorial posts in comparative linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Basel and the University of Neuchâtel.

Max Kaltenmark (1910–2002) was a scholar in sinology and religious studies. He served as head of the Centre Franco-Chinois d'Études Sinologiques, director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient, and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Paris.

Linguistics and religious studies scholar Max Leopold Margolis (1866–1932) earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University. He held academic posts at Columbia, Hebrew Union College, the University of California, and Dropsie College, where he held the chair of biblical philology.

Indologist Max Lindenau studied at the universities of Munich and Greifswald before earning his Ph.D. under Ernst Windisch at the University of Leipzig in 1913. He later served as Privatdozent at the University of Marburg from 1919 to 1927.

Max Oidtmann is a historian, sinologist, and tibetologist who studied at Carleton College, Indiana University, and Harvard University under Mark Elliott. He held faculty posts at Georgetown University, Georgetown University in Qatar, and the University of Munich.

Max Scheler (1874–1928) was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Munich, Berlin, and Jena. He held academic posts at the universities of Jena, Munich, Göttingen, and Cologne, and taught Edward Conze.
